PingLoom

Design Atlas · v1 · 21 Oct 2026

Every important event. One place. Every screen.

The complete UI/UX plan for PingLoom: every page of the Android app, iOS app and web dashboard, every notification and email, and the design system that ties them together. It's built on the PRD v1.0 and drawn as high-fidelity mockups.

P0 · MVP must ship P1 · Paid beta designed, ships later P2 · Later concept only
3surfaces: Android, iOS, Web
60+distinct pages & views planned
216hi-fi frames · 73 in dark mode
40+notification, push & email templates

00 · Overview

The plan at a glance

What we're building, in what order and on which surface, before you scroll into the pixels. Each surface below links to its section. Every mockup's caption lists the screen's purpose, its behaviours and the states it has to handle.

Three surfaces, one product

P0 · MVP

Android app

Kotlin + Jetpack Compose + Material 3. The receiver: it signs in, registers the device with FCM and shows the inbox, event detail and Acknowledge.

  • 4 tabs: Inbox · Projects · Device · Account
  • Android 13+ permission priming and recovery
  • Works offline from a cached inbox
See 30+ Android screens →
P0 · MVP

Web: site + dashboard

Next.js + TypeScript. The system of record for setup: workspace, projects, channels, API keys, playground, event explorer and admin.

  • Public site, docs, pricing in INR
  • Guided "first alert in 5 minutes" checklist
  • Honest per-device delivery states
See the web pages →
P2 · Later

iOS app

SwiftUI with APNs. iOS is P2 in the PRD, but it's designed here with full parity so the product feels premium from day one and the iOS build doesn't need a redesign.

  • Large titles, inset lists, glass tab bar
  • Time-sensitive alerts for high priority
  • Widgets and Live Activity concepts
See 30+ iOS screens →

One status language everywhere

Every surface uses the same words from PRD §9. Reading and acknowledging are separate signals, and "delivered" never appears, because FCM accepting a message doesn't prove the phone displayed it.

accepted→ queued→
provider_accepted retrying · 2/5 failed
User signals:seenacknowledged
Pills always pair colour with a text label, so status never depends on colour alone.

Design decisions to confirm

Brand name & domain

"PingLoom" is provisional (PRD §19). The atlas uses pingloom.dev as a placeholder.

Recommend: clear the trademark and Play Store name before the icon and wordmark are final.

Android Dynamic Color

Material You could re-tint the app from the wallpaper.

Recommend: off by default, so indigo and marigold carry the meaning of priority and "ping". Offer it as a setting later.

Web inbox

The phone is the inbox in the MVP, and the web has the Event explorer.

Recommend: add a personal web inbox in P1, reusing the event card.

iOS timing

iOS is P2 in the PRD but fully designed here.

Recommend: keep the API device model platform-neutral now (platform: android|ios), so APNs is an adapter rather than a rewrite.

Lock-screen preview default

The PRD wants minimal previews by default.

Recommend: default to "Minimal" (project, channel and priority only), with a per-user opt-in to "Full".

Billing surfaces

Play policy limits purchase prompts inside the app.

Recommend: the apps show read-only usage plus a "Manage on the web" link, with no upgrade buttons.

01 · Foundations

The PingLoom design system

Colour, type, space, icons, components and motion for the Android app, the iOS app and the web dashboard. Every other section of this atlas is built from the tokens and parts on this page, in light and in dark.

The theme story: Neel & Genda

Two dyes, one cloth. Neel is indigo, the oldest blue in Indian textiles. Genda is marigold, the flower of every doorway and festival garland. A loom needs both a steady warp and a bright weft, and so does a notification product: a calm system that stays out of the way, and one clear signal when something needs you.

PingLoom

Every important event. One place.

PingLoom turns the events your systems already produce into a calm shared inbox and a push that earns its buzz. Send your first real notification to your phone in under five minutes.

Neel · --primaryGenda · --accentMadder · --highNeem · --success
Indigo is the calm system

Navigation, primary actions, links and normal priority. It reads as trustworthy and quiet, and it has an unusually strong dark-mode twin (periwinkle on indigo night).

Marigold is the ping

Unread dots, the new-event highlight and the retrying state. Because it is rare, the eye goes to it first. If everything is marigold, nothing is.

The loom is the structure

Warp and weft become the .weave texture on hero, empty and onboarding surfaces, and the delivery history is drawn as a thread with knots.

India-first, not India-themed

Linen and dye colours feel local without costumes. Prices are in INR, times are in IST, and the copy avoids idioms so it localises cleanly later.

The mark and the wordmark

Two arcs and a dot: a marigold ping travelling along an indigo thread, inside a rounded indigo tile. The wordmark is PingLoom in Bricolage Grotesque 700 with -2% tracking, one word, capital P and L.

App icon

The icon drops the outer tile (the platform supplies it) and keeps the arcs and dot on a full-bleed indigo field. iOS gets the continuous rounded square, Android gets an adaptive icon: the glyph sits inside the central 66% safe zone so any launcher mask (circle, squircle, teardrop) keeps it intact. A monochrome layer is supplied for Android 13 themed icons.

Rounded square, 22.37% radius. No transparency, no baked-in shadow.

Directions we explored and rejected

Before settling on Neel & Genda we ran the UI UX Pro Max palette search for "developer notification SaaS" and sketched three serious alternatives. Each was applied to the same event row and primary button to see how it behaved in a real screen, not just as a swatch.

#2563EB#6366F1#059669#F8FAFC
Messenger Blue
Send testNormalAcknowledged
Deploy succeeded: api v2.14.0

The database default for this product type, and the safest. But it is generic SaaS blue and indistinguishable from a dozen tools in the same browser tab bar.

Lost: no identity
#0F172A#22C55E#1E293B#94A3B8
Terminal Night
Send testAcknowledgedRun
Deploy succeeded: api v2.14.0

Slate with run-green is the dev-tool cliché. Worse, the brand colour and the "success" meaning are the same green, so a primary button looks like a good result.

Lost: clashes with success
#9A3412#F5EFE6#C2410C#D6A77A
Madder Clay
Send testHighNormal
Payment failures spiking

Warm, earthy and distinctive. But terracotta as the brand colour fights high-priority alerts: a "High" badge and the primary button become the same colour family.

Lost: red is reserved for alerts
Why Neel & Genda wins
  • Every semantic colour has its own hue. Indigo = system, marigold = signal, madder = urgent, neem = done, slate = quiet. None of them overlaps.
  • The brand colour is not an alert colour. You can tell a primary button from a failure at a glance, in either theme.
  • It is ownable. Indigo with marigold is distinctive in a category of blue and green, and it carries a story rooted in the product name and the market.
  • It survives dark mode. The indigo night palette keeps hue and warmth instead of dropping to cold grey, and marigold gets brighter, not duller, on dark.

Colour tokens

Every colour in the product is a CSS variable from base.css, defined for light ("linen") and dark ("indigo night"). Components reference tokens, never hex, so dark mode is a theme switch and not a redesign. Swatches below are painted with the live tokens. Shadows and the focus ring are covered in the elevation sub-part; the scrim is rgba(15,13,34,.42) light and rgba(0,0,0,.6) dark.

Rule: --fg-subtle is never used for text. It measures about 3.4:1 on linen, so it is for non-text only: dividers, disabled icon strokes, placeholder glyphs. Placeholder text uses --fg-muted. Where a soft fill needs text, use the matching -ink token.

Priority mapping

Only three priorities exist: low, normal, high. Priority never relies on colour alone; every badge carries a dot and a word.

Status mapping

The delivery vocabulary comes straight from the PRD. seen and acknowledged are separate things, and the word "delivered" never appears because a push provider accepting a message is not the same as a phone receiving it.

Light
accepted
NeutralThe API validated and stored the event. Nothing has been sent yet.
queued
IndigoWaiting for a worker to hand it to the push provider.
provider_accepted
Neem greenFCM or APNs accepted it. We never call this delivered.
retrying
MarigoldA provider attempt failed. Another is scheduled.
failed
MadderRetries are exhausted. Shows the reason and a manual retry.
seen
SlateOpened on a device. Per person.
acknowledged
Neem greenOne shared state per event, with the person's name.
Dark
accepted
NeutralThe API validated and stored the event. Nothing has been sent yet.
queued
IndigoWaiting for a worker to hand it to the push provider.
provider_accepted
Neem greenFCM or APNs accepted it. We never call this delivered.
retrying
MarigoldA provider attempt failed. Another is scheduled.
failed
MadderRetries are exhausted. Shows the reason and a manual retry.
seen
SlateOpened on a device. Per person.
acknowledged

Typography

Three families, each with one job. Bricolage Grotesque brings a slightly hand-cut, woven character to headings. Geist is neutral, dense-friendly UI text. Geist Mono carries everything a developer copies: keys, ULIDs, curl and timestamps.

Display, page titles, dialog titles, empty-state titles, the wordmark. Always -1% to -3% tracking.

Aa

Geist · 400, 500, 600

All interface text: body, labels, buttons, tables, inputs. Tabular numerals on counts and prices.

Aa

Geist Mono · 400, 500

API keys, IDs, code, timestamps, status pills and eyebrows. Never for paragraphs.

Mobile uses the platform type

The apps do not ship the web scale as-is. iOS uses SF Pro and honours Dynamic Type up to the accessibility sizes (layouts reflow, nothing is truncated with a fixed height). Android uses Geist mapped onto the Material 3 type scale, with Roboto Flex as the fallback if the font fails to load; sizes are in sp and follow the system font scale. Geist Mono is used on both for keys, IDs and timestamps.

Spacing, radii, elevation and grid

Spacing scale

Built on a 4px base. Component interiors use --s-1 to --s-4; layout gaps use --s-6 and up.

Radii

Larger containers get larger radii, nested corners step down by the padding (a 16px card with 12px padding holds an 8px control).

--r-xs6px · Status pills, focus ring
--r-sm8px · Buttons, inputs
--r-md12px · Callouts, code
--r-lg16px · Cards, event rows
--r-xl22px · Sheets, hero panels
--r-2xl28px · Large sheets
--r-pillfull · Chips, badges, avatars

Elevation

Three levels, soft and indigo-tinted in light, deeper and black in dark. Borders carry most of the separation; shadow is for things that float. The focus ring is 0 0 0 3px of 35% primary and sits outside any shadow.

  • 16px side margin on phones, 24px on tablets and foldables.
  • Touch targets are 44 × 44 (48dp on Android) with at least 8px between neighbours. A 24px icon gets padding, not a bigger glyph.
  • Safe areas win. Nothing sits under the status bar, the Dynamic Island, the home indicator or the gesture bar; content scrolls under them, controls never do.
  • Bottom navigation has 4 items or fewer in PingLoom (Inbox, Projects, Devices, Settings), never more than 5.

Iconography

PingLoom uses the Lucide family because it is open, consistent and available natively on every platform we target. Every icon sits on a 24px grid with a 2px live-area padding, a 1.75px stroke, round caps and joins, and no fill. They inherit currentColor.

24 grid, 2px paddingKeyline shapes: circle 20, square 18, portrait 16 × 20.
16 / 20 / 24 sizes16 inline in text, 20 in buttons and rows, 24 in bars. Stroke stays 1.75 at every size.
RulesIcons never carry meaning alone: pair with a label, or give an icon-only control an aria-label. No emoji as icons, ever. No filled variants except the unread dot.

The event card is the most important component in the product: it appears in the inbox, project views, search results and the notification detail header, so it is specified first and in the most detail.

Event card anatomy. Unread dot (marigold, 8px) · title (15px, 700 when unread, 600 when read) · relative time (mono) · two-line body preview · channel with hash icon · project with folder icon · priority badge. High priority adds a 3px madder bar on the left edge. Unread adds a faint marigold wash and border. Motion

Motion explains cause and effect and never decorates. Most transitions are one of three durations, with an ease-out on the way in and a faster ease-in on the way out. The only expressive animation in the product is the ping.

150 ms · fast
Hover, press, chip toggle, checkbox, all exits (toast, menu, dialog)
220 ms · default
Enter of toast, menu, dialog, new row insert, drawer on desktop
360 ms · slow
Bottom sheet, page and onboarding step transitions, hero reveal
Ping ripple
One expanding marigold ring, 600 ms, played once
Enter · ease-outcubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1)Fast start, soft landing. --ease-out
Exit · ease-incubic-bezier(.4, 0, 1, 1)Leaves quickly, no lingering.
Exit faster than enter. Things appear at 220 ms and leave at 150 ms (about 70%). A sheet that enters in 360 ms leaves in 220 ms. People wait for what is coming, not for what they dismissed. Only animate transform and opacity; never width, height or top.

The ping

When a new event arrives while the app is open, the unread dot in its row emits one marigold ripple (scale to 5x while fading, 600 ms, ease-out) and the row slides in by 8px. It plays once per event, never loops, and never plays for events that were already there when the screen opened. The demo below repeats every 4.5 seconds only so you can watch it.

02 · Notifications

Every notification PingLoom sends

What travels through FCM and APNs, how priority becomes sound and interruption, how each push looks on Android and iOS, the in-app and dashboard moments, the permission journey, the transactional emails, every line of copy, and the words the UI may use to describe delivery.

1 · Notification anatomy and privacy model

A push is a doorbell, not a letter. The message that crosses Google's or Apple's servers carries just enough to ring the right bell and to find the event again: an event ID, a title, a priority and a channel. The body, the data object, the action link and the acknowledgement state are fetched by the app after it authenticates. This follows PRD §9 ("the mobile app retrieves complete content via authenticated API") and §14 ("keep lock-screen notification previews minimal by default"). P0 · MVP

#PartComes fromIn payload?
1Small icon, app nameApp resources, fixedNo
2Line 1: "PingLoom · agents"channel slug, formatted on deviceYes (channel)
3Line 2: "New high-priority event"Local string chosen from priorityYes (priority)
4TimeDevice clock when receivedNo
5Actions: Acknowledge, OpenDefined in the app. Acknowledge calls the API with the stored sessionNo
6Tap intentevent_idYes
7Channel and heads-uppriority maps to a channel IDYes
 
// FCM HTTP v1, data message. Sent by the PingLoom worker only.
{ "message": {
    "token": "<device token, never logged>",
    "data": {
      "event_id": "01JEXK7Q9W3RZ5M2B8H4TQ6N1D",
      "title":    "Agent approval required",
      "priority": "high",
      "channel":  "agents",
      "group":    "ws_acme-labs"   // bundling key, no names
    },
    "android": { "priority": "HIGH" }
} }
// APNs (P2). The visible text is already the Minimal string,
// so the OS shows a safe preview even if the extension fails.
{ "aps": {
    "alert": { "title": "PingLoom · agents", "body": "New high-priority event" },
    "interruption-level": "time-sensitive",
    "thread-id": "ws_acme-labs",
    "mutable-content": 1 },
  "event_id": "01JEXK7Q9W3RZ5M2B8H4TQ6N1D", "t": "Agent approval required" }

Who sees what

Your serverPOST /v1/notifications with pl_live_… key
PingLoom APIStores event + outbox, replies 202
WorkerOne delivery per active device. Service credentials stay here
FCM / APNsSees the payload above and nothing else
PingLoom appBuilds the notification. On tap or on Full mode it authenticates and fetches

Trust boundary: the highlighted FCM / APNs node sees only the payload shown above. Everything to its right is fetched over HTTPS with the member's own session.

In the payload (leaves PingLoom)

  • event_id: a ULID, useless without a signed-in member of the workspace
  • title: max 120 characters. Developers are told titles transit FCM and APNs, so they should not put secrets in them
  • priority, channel: choose the Android channel or iOS interruption level, and the text
  • group: an opaque workspace key used to bundle notifications

Fetched after authentication

  • Full body (up to 2,000 characters) and the data object (up to 8 KB)
  • action_url, validated as HTTPS. Unsafe links are shown and need confirmation, never auto-opened
  • Source, project, occurred_at, delivery attempts, acknowledgement and recipients
  • Workspace membership is checked on every deep link. A non-member sees "You don't have access to this event"

Never sent in a push

  • API keys, key prefixes, session or refresh tokens
  • FCM service-account credentials or other devices' tokens
  • Email addresses, teammate names, payment data
  • The full body, data and action_url, unless the user opts into Full preview (they are then fetched on-device, still not placed in the payload)

Lock-screen preview modes

One setting per user, in Account, Notification preferences. It controls how much text the app puts in the OS notification, on the lock screen and in the shade. Minimal is the default and needs no network. Title only reads title from the payload. Full is opt-in: the app wakes, authenticates with its stored session, fetches the event and builds the notification locally. On iOS this needs a notification service extension (mutable-content). If the fetch fails or times out, both platforms fall back to Minimal, never to a blank or raw payload.

Open decision for the owner. Titles are in the payload so that Title-only works instantly and offline, but Minimal ignores them on the device. If a project's titles may be sensitive, a per-project "never put titles in pushes" option would make Title-only fetch like Full does. It is cheap to add before launch and awkward after.

2 · Priority to channel mapping

Priority is only low | normal | high and it decides, per platform, how loudly a push arrives. Android channels are created once at install and then belong to the user: they can change sound or importance in system settings, so the app never assumes its defaults still apply. P0 · Android P2 · iOS

PingLoom priorityAndroid channel and importanceSound and vibrationHeads-up and lock screenFCM priorityiOS interruption levelAPNs

IMPORTANCE_LOW		 Silent. No vibration No heads-up. Sits in the shade's Silent section; hidden from the lock screen by default NORMAL Passive
passive: no sound, no screen wake, lands quietly in Notification Center		 Priority 5

Rules that keep the mapping honest

  • Channels are created once, with stable IDs (pingloom_high, pingloom_normal, pingloom_low). Renaming a channel in the UI never changes its ID.
  • If a user lowers a channel in system settings, the Device status screen shows "High priority alerts are set to silent in Android settings" with a link to the channel page.
  • PingLoom does not request iOS Critical Alerts or Android's Do Not Disturb bypass. Time Sensitive is the ceiling.
  • The tags "high", "normal" and "low" always appear as text beside a dot, never colour alone.
  • One event creates one notification per active device; a second device never doubles the quota count (FR-08).

Quiet hours are P1 P1 · Paid beta

Per PRD §4, quiet hours mute alerts between two times the user picks, except for an opted-in urgent category. Until it ships, no quiet-hours control appears in the app.

Low
Normal
High
00:0007:0012:0022:0024:00
  • Hatched hours (22:00 to 07:00 IST): low and normal arrive silently in the inbox, with no sound and no heads-up. They are posted on the low channel, so nothing is lost.
  • High arrives normally only if the user opted that category in as urgent. Otherwise it is silent too, and the owner sees a one-line note in Settings when quiet hours would hold high events.
  • Do Not Disturb and Focus belong to the OS. PingLoom works with them and never tries to bypass them.

3 · Android push mockups

Five moments, each at 412×915 logical size. Different frames show different preview modes on purpose; a real device shows exactly one, chosen in settings. All actions are real: Acknowledge calls POST /v1/events/{id}/acknowledge with the stored session (the phone must be unlocked first), Open deep-links after a membership check. P0 · MVP

4 · iOS push mockups

iOS and APNs are P2 in the PRD (§4: "iOS/APNs, web push… Later"). These frames are design intent so that Android decisions do not paint iOS into a corner. Nothing here ships in the MVP, and no iOS control may appear in the product until the backend delivers it. P2 · Later

Frosted-material cards, SF-style type, a 38 pt app icon and the iOS interruption levels from the mapping table. Previews use Title only where a title helps the story; the Minimal string is the default.

5 · In-app notifications

When PingLoom is open, the app talks for itself. The rule from PRD §6: in the foreground, update the inbox and show a system notification "according to user preferences without duplicates". PingLoom's default is no system notification while the app is in the foreground; the event arrives as an in-app banner and a new inbox row instead. P0 · MVP

Web dashboard toasts

Toasts confirm an action the user just took. They stack top right, last 5 s (8 s when they hold an action), pause on hover and focus, and are announced through role="status". Errors that block the user stay inline next to the field. A toast never says more than the system knows (see section 9).

6 · Permission priming

Android 13+ makes notification permission a runtime prompt, and after two denials the system stops showing it. iOS asks exactly once. So PingLoom never fires the system dialog cold: a priming screen explains the value first, and only Allow notifications triggers the real prompt. "Not now" is always available and always leads to a working inbox. The prompt appears after sign-in and workspace selection (Journey A step 4), never on first launch. P0 · Android 13+ P2 · iOS

7 · Transactional emails

Email is for things a person must act on outside the app: verifying, recovering, joining, and for security and usage notices. It is never a campaign channel (PRD §4 excludes email marketing). Style: linen background, a white card with a 5 px indigo and marigold bar, Bricolage headings, one clear indigo call to action, mono for IDs and key prefixes. Plain-text twins are generated from the same copy, links are always HTTPS, and no email contains an API key, a session token or an event body. Each frame shows the subject and preheader the inbox list would show.

8 · Notification copy library

Every system and product notification, with the words an engineer should ship. Titles are sentence case and under 60 characters; bodies say what happened, what it means and what to do, in one or two sentences. Priority is the PingLoom priority used when the notification becomes a push (low, normal, high); in-app and email rows use it for urgency and ordering. Surfaces: push in-app email dashboard. Where a row is a push, the lock screen shows the Minimal text from section 1 unless the user chose another mode. Nothing here says "delivered".

9 · Delivery-truth rules

PRD §9: "Provider acceptance does not mean device delivery or user reading. For MVP, do not label an event 'delivered' unless there is genuine delivery evidence." PingLoom has evidence for exactly four things, in order. Every status chip, toast, email and doc sentence must claim no more than the highest step actually reached. P0 · MVP

1
API accepted
accepted queued

The request was valid, the event and outbox row are committed, and the API replied 202 with an event ID.

Evidence

Database commit. Nothing has left PingLoom yet.

UI may say

"Event accepted", "Queued"

2
Sent to FCM
provider_accepted retrying failed

Google's FCM returned success for a device token. One record per device. Transient errors retry with backoff; permanent errors fail.

Evidence

FCM response, stored per delivery attempt.

UI may say

"Sent to FCM", "Retrying, attempt 2 of 5", "Failed to reach FCM"

3
Seen on device
seen

The app on this person's device opened the event, or reported it was shown, and told the server. Personal to each member.

Evidence

An authenticated "seen" call from that device.

UI may say

"Seen by you", "Seen on Pixel 8"

4
Acknowledged
acknowledged

A member pressed Acknowledge. One shared state per event, with the person and time.

Evidence

An authenticated acknowledge call, recorded once.

UI may say

"Acknowledged by Vikram Shah, 09:32 IST"

The gaps are the point. Between 1 and 2, our own queue or FCM can fail. Between 2 and 3, the phone may be off, offline, in battery saver, force-stopped, blocked by permission or silenced by Focus. FCM accepting a message is a receipt from Google, not from the phone. Nothing on the server can prove step 3 without the app reporting it.
Words the UI may use
  • Acceptedthe API committed the event (202)
  • Queuedwaiting for the worker
  • Sent to FCMFCM returned success for that device
  • Retrying, attempt 2 of 5a transient provider error
  • Failed to reach FCMretries exhausted, or a permanent error
  • Seen by you Seen on Pixel 8only when the app reported it
  • Acknowledged by Vikram Shahshared, named, timestamped
  • Device readythe server confirmed registration
Words the UI must not use
  • DeliveredFCM acceptance is not device delivery (PRD §9)
  • Sent to your phoneit was sent to FCM, not to the phone
  • Received Arrivedunless the app reported "seen"
  • Notified Alertedclaims the human noticed
  • Guaranteed Instant Real-timeno SLA exists (PRD §2.3)
  • Success Donealone, on a send. Say which step succeeded
  • Readfor provider status. "Seen" and "Read" are per-user app states
  • Readyfor a device before server confirmation

The same moment, written right and wrong

Event accepted, waiting for FCMWe'll update this to "Sent to FCM" when Google confirms. That isn't confirmation it reached the phone.
Sent to FCMAccepted for 2 devices at 09:30:03 IST. Open the event to see when each one reports it.

Right. Names the step reached, offers the next, and says what it does not prove.

Notification delivered!Your message was sent to your phone successfully.
SuccessEveryone on your team has been notified.

Wrong, struck through. Claims delivery, a person and a result that PingLoom cannot prove. These strings are lint-checked: the build fails if "delivered" appears in user-facing copy.

Where the rule bites. Dashboard event pills use only the .status vocabulary above. The setup guide's last step reads "Seen on device", not "Delivered". The email digest says "failed to reach FCM". The quick-start success state says "Accepted", then "Sent to FCM", then waits for the phone to say "Seen".

Launch and auth

From cold start to a verified account. Every screen has inline validation and a way out when offline or rate-limited.

Onboarding and permission

Three short welcome pages, then a primer before the Android 13 system prompt, then device registration. The device is only called Ready after the server says so.

Inbox (home)

The inbox is the product on a phone. It stays usable when notifications are denied and when the network is gone.

Event detail

Everything an event carries, with one decisive action. Acknowledging is shared; reading is personal.

Projects and channels

Read-only browsing of the workspace plus the one thing members control here: which channels ping them.

Device status

A quick answer to "will this phone ping me?", with a real test and the exact failure when it won't.

Account and settings

Profile, workspace, notification privacy and the two guarded exits.

P1 screens

Team invitations and read-only usage. Both are designed now so the P0 navigation does not need rework when they ship.

Android-specific notes

Edge-to-edge and insets P0 · MVP

Targets API 35, so the app always draws behind system bars: enableEdgeToEdge() in the activity and WindowInsets.safeDrawing in Compose.

  • Top bars use statusBars padding; the navigation bar and sticky Acknowledge bar use navigationBars so nothing sits under the gesture handle.
  • The IME pushes forms up with imePadding(); primary buttons stay visible above the keyboard.
  • Display cutouts and punch-holes: content starts below the status bar. Landscape and foldables use displayCutout insets.

Predictive back P0 · MVP

android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" with Navigation Compose back handlers, so the shrinking-screen preview works on Android 14+.

  • Bottom sheets and dialogs consume back first; the filter sheet previews dismissal.
  • Back on a top-level tab returns to Inbox, then exits. Welcome pages go back one page.
  • Unsaved input (Delete confirmation, forms) uses a BackHandler with a discard confirmation only when needed.

Dynamic Color: off by default P0 · MVP

Decision: brand palette always, no wallpaper-derived colours.

  • Priority and state colours (madder, neem, marigold) carry meaning. A wallpaper palette could turn "high" teal or clash with "acknowledged".
  • Neel and Genda also match the web and iOS apps, which keeps support screenshots consistent.
  • Both brand schemes are tested for 4.5:1 text contrast; Dynamic Color gives no such guarantee.
  • Later option: an opt-in "Use wallpaper colours" switch that recolours only surfaces and keeps semantic colours fixed.
NeelGendaMadderNeemLinen

Widget concept P2 · Later

Glance widgets built with Glance (Compose). Not part of the first release. Tapping opens the event through the same deep link and membership check.

Inbox2unread · 1 high
HighPayment failures spiking9 min ago

SDK targets P0 · MVP

  • minSdk 26 (Android 8.0): notification channels are native and desugaring is minimal; covers the vast majority of active devices in India.
  • targetSdk: always the latest stable release, which Play requires each year. compileSdk equals target.
  • Below API 33 the notification permission is implicit, so the primer is skipped.
  • Kotlin, Compose BOM, Material 3, Navigation Compose, Room for the cache, WorkManager for registration and read sync, Firebase Messaging.

Accessibility checks done P0 · MVP

  • TalkBack: every icon button has a contentDescription. Event rows merge into one node: "Agent approval required, high priority, Recon Agent agents, 2 minutes ago, unread". Switches expose name and state.
  • Targets: all interactive elements are at least 48 dp with 8 dp spacing; chips and list rows meet it through padding.
  • Font scaling to 200%: layouts use sp, flexible rows and wrapping, no fixed heights on text. At 200% the chip row scrolls, event cards grow, and the Acknowledge bar stays pinned.
  • Colour: text is at least 4.5:1 in both themes; priority and state are always also conveyed by an icon and a label.
  • Motion: shimmer and cross-fades honour "Remove animations".

04 · iOS app

iOS app

A native SwiftUI app that mirrors every Android P0 screen with full parity, but speaks iOS: large titles, inset-grouped lists, Liquid Glass chrome, detent sheets and swipe actions. P2 · Later The PRD lists iOS/APNs as a later release, so this section is the design to build against when it is approved.

Why iOS feels different here

Same product, same words, same states. What changes is the grammar: navigation, how things slide up, how lists look, and how loud a notification may be. The glass material is used only for navigation and controls (tab bar, nav buttons, bottom action bar); content stays opaque for contrast. Colour is restrained: indigo is the tint; marigold appears only for the unread dot and ping signals.

PatternAndroid (Compose, Material 3)iOS (SwiftUI)
NavigationBottom NavigationBar (4 destinations) plus a top app bar per screen.Floating Liquid Glass tab bar (TabView): Inbox, Projects, Device, Settings. Each tab owns a NavigationStack with a large title that collapses.
BackSystem back gesture / button; up arrow in the top bar.Left-edge swipe plus a glass back button. The previous title can label it. Never a hamburger.
SheetsModal bottom sheet or full-screen dialog.Sheets with detents (.medium, .large) and a grabber; swipe down to dismiss. Sign-out uses confirmationDialog, errors use alert.
ListsMaterial cards with dividers, filled chips.Inset-grouped List: 14pt rounded groups, hairline separators inset 16pt, 44pt minimum rows, swipe actions and context menus.
TypeRoboto-style scale in sp. System font scale.SF Pro with Dynamic Type text styles (largeTitle, headline, body, footnote), supported to AX5 so rows reflow.
HapticsSelective vibration (HapticFeedbackConstant).UIImpact / UISelection / UINotificationFeedbackGenerator, used sparingly: tick on selection, success on acknowledge, warning on destructive.
Notification levelsChannels by importance: low, default, high (heads-up).Interruption levels: low = passive, normal = active, high = time-sensitive. Critical alerts are not used (needs Apple approval).
PermissionAndroid 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime prompt after our primer.One-shot system alert after our primer. If denied, only Settings can change it, so we deep-link to it.
Search / filterSearch bar and filter chips on screen..searchable in the nav bar with scopes; filters in a native Menu.
Scope note. iOS is P2 in the PRD (§4). Every screen is tagged P2, and P1 features (search, invites, usage) carry both. Sign in with Apple is deliberately not drawn as a control. Widgets, Live Activities and alternate icons are concepts beyond the PRD.

06 · Web dashboard

Web dashboard: setup and projects

The signed-in Next.js dashboard at app.pingloom.dev: the app shell every page shares, the onboarding wizard and Getting started checklist, the Overview, projects and channels, API keys, the API playground and devices. Event explorer, team, webhooks, billing, settings and error pages follow the same shell in section 07.

Dashboard IA and app shell

The dashboard is one Next.js app at app.pingloom.dev. Navigation is project-scoped on top, workspace-scoped below the divider: the sidebar items above the line (Overview to Devices) act on the project chosen in the top bar breadcrumb, and the items below (Team, Webhooks, Billing, Settings) act on the whole workspace. Every page in this section and in section 07 sits inside the shell defined here.

Onboarding wizard and Getting started

After email verification, a three-step full-page wizard creates the workspace, the first project (My First Project, with channel general created for you) and sets the environment. It lands on Getting started, a persistent checklist. The checklist deliberately separates three facts that are easy to blur: API accepted (our server stored the event), Sent to FCM (Firebase accepted it, i.e. provider_accepted), and Seen on device (the app opened or fetched it). We never claim the phone received it until the app reports it.

Overview

The landing page once setup is done: what happened today, how much quota is left, and whether delivery is healthy. Delivery health only ever reports provider states (provider_accepted, retrying, failed); the word “delivered” is never used, because Firebase acceptance is not proof of display on the phone.

Projects

Owners and admins create, rename and archive projects; members see only projects with channels they subscribe to. A project belongs to one environment and one workspace; slugs are unique per workspace (unique(workspace_id, slug)).

Project detail

One project, four tabs. Channels and Members are management surfaces for owners and admins (members see them read-only); Recent events is a short live feed that links to the full explorer; Integration quick start gives a copy-paste request that works with the project’s key.

API keys

Keys belong to a project and are visible to owners and admins only (GET/POST /v1/projects/{id}/keys). The list never reveals a secret: just name, prefix, scopes, creator and last use. The plaintext appears exactly once, in a modal that cannot be dismissed by accident. Rotation and revocation take effect immediately (FR-03).

API playground

Send a real event from the dashboard without leaving the browser. The form builds the request live; the response panel then follows the event through the status vocabulary, one device at a time. It uses the authenticated dashboard endpoint (POST /v1/projects/{id}/test), so it works before the user has copied any key.

Devices

Devices are personal: they are the Android phones where the signed-in user has registered an FCM token. The page explains health in words and offers the one lifecycle action the API supports, DELETE /v1/devices/{id} (deactivate).

07 · Web dashboard

Events, team and admin

The operator side of PingLoom at app.pingloom.dev: finding and debugging events, watching quota, managing people, webhook sources and billing, configuring the workspace, and every failure state in between. Each frame recreates the app shell (240px sidebar, 56px top bar) so it reads as one product.

Event explorer P0 · MVP

The system of record for “what did we send, and where did it get to”. It is tenant-scoped, ordered by created_at, id and paginated by cursor so a million-row workspace stays fast (FR-12). Every status pill uses the PRD vocabulary (accepted, queued, provider_accepted, retrying, failed), because provider acceptance is not proof that a phone showed the message.

Event detail P0 · MVP

One event, end to end. The delivery attempts are drawn as a vertical thread: each knot is a state the server actually recorded, sub-knots are one row per device. Nothing here claims the phone showed the message; “seen” and “acknowledged” are separate, later knots.

Usage and quotas P1 · Paid beta

Plain-language metering so nobody is surprised by a 429. Accepted events are counted exactly once from a transactional ledger; seats and rate limits are enforced separately (FR-10).

Team P1 · Paid beta

Journey B’s admin side: invite, assign a role, revoke, remove. Roles come straight from PRD §12 (owner / admin / member); the UI never offers an action the server would refuse.

Webhook sources P1 · Paid beta

Journey C: an owner creates a source, gets a one-time signing secret, and an external service POSTs JSON that an approved template turns into a normal event. Bad signatures, bad payloads and floods are rejected and logged without leaking secrets (FR-15).

Billing P1 · Paid beta

Business billing on the web through a hosted checkout and portal (PRD §12). The dashboard never renders a card form. Subscription state changes only from verified provider webhooks, and the whole area is labelled as test mode until the real provider integration is finished (FR-14).

Settings P0 · MVP

Five tabs: Workspace, Profile, Notifications, Privacy and data, Audit log. Destructive actions need typed confirmation and are blocked with an explanation when they can’t succeed.

System states gallery P0 · MVP

Every state the PRD calls out (§7 UX rule): expired session, forbidden, not found, rate limited, service error, maintenance, degraded provider and offline. Each says what happened, whether data is safe, and the one next step.
